note.text:
• Electric bulb (filament lamp): current heats a thin tungsten filament until it glows (electrical → light and heat). LED bulbs use much less energy.
• Electric iron: current flows through a heating element; a thermostat (a bimetallic strip) switches it off when it is hot enough and on again when it cools.
• Electric fan: an electric motor turns the blades (electrical → kinetic energy).
• Refrigerator: a pump moves a cooling liquid that takes heat from inside and releases it at the back.
• Radio: receives radio waves and changes them into sound in the loudspeaker.
• Torch: a battery (chemical energy) lights a bulb when the switch closes the circuit.
Energy used = power × time; an appliance of high power uses more energy.

worked_example.problem: Why does an electric iron not keep getting hotter and hotter?
steps: It has a thermostat (a bimetallic strip).
When the iron is hot enough, the strip bends and switches the current off; when it cools, it switches it on again.
worked_example.answer: The thermostat switches the current off and on to keep the temperature steady.

cards.idea: A filament bulb turns electrical energy into light and heat.
A thermostat switches a heater off when it is hot enough.
A motor turns electrical energy into movement (kinetic energy).

pick.q: What keeps the temperature of an electric iron steady?
e: The plug connects to the socket.
pick.y: It switches the current off and on.

pick.q: Why are LED bulbs better than filament bulbs?
pick.r: They use much less energy for the same light.
pick.y: Less energy is wasted as heat.

right.text: A radio changes waves into sound.
A fridge removes heat from inside.

wrong.text: A refrigerator makes cold by adding ice from outside.
wrong.explain: It pumps heat from inside to the back.

wrong.text: A thermostat makes an iron hotter and hotter without stopping.
wrong.explain: It switches it off when hot enough.

wrong.text: A filament bulb turns light into electricity.
wrong.explain: It turns electricity into light and heat.
